scenario.name: Sandworm ArguePatch Loader & CaddyWiper Domain-Aware Disk Wiper (T1561.001)
scenario.overview: Imagine a cunning saboteur operating inside a company headquarters who deliberately spares the central dispatch tower itself so the tower stays alive long enough to broadcast destruction orders to every branch office. Using a disguised repair-tool wrapper pushed from the central policy board, the wiper checks whether each machine is the dispatch tower first; on every regular office computer, it seizes ownership of every user drawer, scrubs every document to blank zeros, and erases the floor plan of every hard drive. In this scenario (T1053.005, Sandworm ArguePatch Loader & CaddyWiper Domain-Aware Disk Wiper (T1561.001)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: gPO Mass Deployment, then dsRoleGetPrimaryDomainInformation Check, then takeOwnership Recursive File Zeroing. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering GPO Mass Deployment, then DsRoleGetPrimaryDomainInformation Check, then TakeOwnership Recursive File Zeroing, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: GPO Mass Deployment & ArguePatch Patched Debugger Loader Execution
stages.subtitle: Execution & Defense Evasion (T1053.005 - Scheduled Task / T1574)
stages.description: Standing inside the central dispatch tower, the saboteur takes a genuinely known software debugger, surgically splices a hidden trigger into its opening routine, and pushes it out across the entire company through the official morning policy board. From a compromised Domain Controller, Sandworm staged payloads in SYSVOL and pushed an Active Directory Group Policy Scheduled Task to execute CaddyWiper either directly (caddy.exe) or wrapped inside ArguePatch (a modified copy of Hex-Rays IDA Pro’s legitimate win32_remote.exe binary where Sandworm patched a single internal function to read, XOR-decrypt, and execute encrypted CaddyWiper shellcode directly in memory). Sandworm reused the exact same ArguePatch loader weeks later during the April 2022 electrical substation attack (Industroyer2) to schedule timed destruction of Windows servers. In the documented EventID 1 exchange from Sandworm GPO Scheduled Task Push to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ACK 1 (confirming that the win32_remote.exe request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 Stage 2: DsRoleGetPrimaryDomainInformation Check to Spare Domain Controllers). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ win32_remote.exe / ⇠#1 ACK 1) from Node ① (#1 Sandworm GPO Scheduled Task Push) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX Zeroing).

stages.title: Stage 2: DsRoleGetPrimaryDomainInformation Check to Spare Domain Controllers
stages.subtitle: Discovery & Execution Guardrails (T1082 / T1480 - Execution Guardrails)
stages.description: Assembling its own command labels secretly piece by piece so casual code scanners read nothing suspicious, the wiper very first action is checking the room nameplate: if it realizes it is standing inside the central dispatch tower, it immediately steps back so the tower stays online to keep wrecking every other room. Resolving API names dynamically on the stack to hide its Import Address Table (IAT), CaddyWiper’s very first action was calling DsRoleGetPrimaryDomainInformation(NULL, DsRolePrimaryDomainInfoBasic, &pInfo) from netapi32.dll (checking whether pInfo->MachineRole == DsRole_RolePrimaryDomainController [value 5], and immediately terminating itself without wiping anything if running on a Primary Domain Controller so Sandworm retained its Active Directory foothold and GPO distribution server). This execution guardrail explains why responders during a CaddyWiper incident often found member workstations and application servers completely bricked while the Primary Domain Controller remained up and actively pushing the malicious GPO. In the documented EDR exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to ArguePatch Loader (Patched win32_remote.exe), ArguePatch Loader (Patched win32_remote.exe) responds with ALERT T1082 (confirming that the Stage 2: DsRoleGetPrimaryDomainInformation Check to Spare Domain Controllers request succeeded on ArguePatch Loader (Patched win32_remote.exe) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 Stage 3: TakeOwnership Recursive File Zeroing & IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX Wipe). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ Stage 2: DsRoleGetPrimaryDomainInformation Check to Spare Domain Controllers / ⇠#2 ALERT T1082) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 ArguePatch Loader (Patched win32_remote.exe)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX Zeroing).

keySpecs.value: Immediately unlink malicious GPOs and isolate the Primary Domain Controller (`PDC`) during a wiper outbreak, as the PDC is intentionally left intact by the malware to act as the distribution engine.

stages.title: Stage 3: TakeOwnership Recursive File Zeroing & IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX Wipe
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1561.001 - Disk Content Wipe / T1561.002 - Disk Structure Wipe)
stages.description: On every ordinary workstation and branch server, the wiper claims legal ownership of every locked desk drawer, overwrites every personal file with blank zeros from top to bottom, and sends a single raw control blast that erases the master partition blueprint of every attached hard drive. On member workstations and servers, CaddyWiper enabled SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege, recursively walked C:\Users and all drives from D:\ to Z:\ calling SetNamedSecurityInfoA (transferring file ownership and DACLs to the current user before overwriting every file’s contents with 0x00 null bytes), and finally looped from \\.\PhysicalDrive9 down to \\.\PhysicalDrive0 issuing DeviceIoControl with IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX (0x0007C054 passing a 1,920-byte zero-filled DRIVE_LAYOUT_INFORMATION_EX structure that instructs the Windows disk driver itself to erase the MBR/GPT partition tables). By abusing the legitimate Windows kernel disk IOCTL IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX (0x0007C054) rather than bringing a third-party kernel driver, CaddyWiper destroyed the disk partition table without needing a BYOVD driver. In the documented EDR exchange from ArguePatch Loader (Patched win32_remote.exe) to CaddyWiper (DsRole Domain Controller Check), CaddyWiper (DsRole Domain Controller Check) responds with ALERT T1561.001 (confirming that the Stage 3: TakeOwnership Recursive File Zeroing & IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX Wipe request succeeded on CaddyWiper (DsRole Domain Controller Check) and completing the final execution objective of Sandworm ArguePatch Loader & CaddyWiper Domain-Aware Disk Wiper (T1561.001)). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Stage 3: TakeOwnership Recursive File Zeroing & IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX Wipe / ⇠#3 ALERT T1561.001) from Node ③ (#3 ArguePatch Loader (Patched win32_remote.exe)) to Node ④ (#4 CaddyWiper (DsRole Domain Controller Check)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX Zeroing).
